subject: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@cloudscale.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Perez <jacob.perez@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics

Hi Rishi,

Thanks — as we review the draft Order Form before approval I need to confirm the security exhibit / audit language we discussed with procurement. Two items we need clarity on:

1) Audit scope & cadence: CloudScale requires the ability to validate controls supporting data security and access for vendors in our supply chain. We typically ask for either a current SOC 2 Type II report or the right to conduct a one-time assessment within the first 12 months. Can you confirm Redwood's position on timing (when you can provide SOC 2 reports) and whether you allow vendor-conducted verification?

2) Pen test evidence and access: For high-risk suppliers we expect either a redacted pen test summary or a third-party attestation plus reasonable evidence (sample logs, remediation timelines). We also want to understand on-site vs remote rights (CloudScale prefers remote where possible).

Could you send the proposed security exhibit and indicate what evidence you can provide, expected delivery windows, and any limits (e.g., no raw logs, confidentiality constraints)? Procurement needs a short memo to justify acceptance.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Regards,
Elena Martinez
Head of Vendor Security
CloudScale Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the current security exhibit we include in Order Forms (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx). Quick answers up-front:

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report on an annual cadence. We can provide the most recent report within 30 days of signature / order form execution.
- Pen test: We can provide a redacted executive summary of our most recent penetration test and a remediation status summary; we do not provide raw exploit logs or attack payloads.
- Audit verification: We prefer to provide written artifacts (SOC 2 report, SSP excerpts, redacted pen-test summary) via a secure portal. We are open to allowing a third-party assessment under a narrow, pre-agreed scope, executed no more than once per 12 months, with costs borne by the customer. On-site access is something we reserve for exceptional cases and would require mutual agreement and reasonable notice.

Marissa — can you please review the exhibit and suggest precise redline language for: (a) auditor appointment/notice period, (b) evidence delivery channel/retention, (c) limits on logs/raw data, and (d) cost allocation for third-party audits. Ben — loop in sales operations for any procurement playbook items.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 09:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics

Rishi / team — reviewed the exhibit. Below are recommended positions and suggested redline snippets you can share with Procurement. I copied Elena so they see the proposed compromise.

1) Audit right -> Verification right: Replace overly broad "audit rights" with a limited "right to reasonably verify compliance with the Security Exhibit". Suggested text: "Customer may, no more than once per 12-month period, engage an independent third-party auditor to verify Redwood's compliance with the Security Exhibit, subject to Redwood's reasonable security and confidentiality requirements."

2) Notice and scope: Require written notice of at least 15 business days and a mutually agreed scope that maps to the controls in the Security Exhibit. Add a requirement that audits be remote by default; on-site visits permitted only for material issues and with mutual agreement.

3) Evidence and delivery: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted penetration test executive summary within 30 days of request. Additional supporting artifacts (sample configurations, control descriptions, redacted evidence excerpts) will be provided via a secure, access-controlled portal for a 12-month retention window. Do not commit to providing raw logs, production data, or exploit payloads.

4) Cost & confidentiality: Customer to bear reasonable third-party auditor fees. All audit materials are confidential and may only be used for internal compliance purposes; auditor must enter Redwood's standard NDA.

5) Post-audit remediation: Redwood will provide a remediation status summary for any confirmed findings and reasonable timelines for remediation, where applicable.

If Elena is okay with this, I'll prepare a tracked redline of the exhibit and the short memo you can attach to the procurement ticket.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx (with comments)

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@cloudscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Perez <jacob.perez@cloudscale.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics

Marissa / Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and InfoSec: 

- Notice period: 15 business days is acceptable, but CloudScale needs the ability to request an on-site review in situations where the onboarding impacts regulated data flows or where a significant finding has been reported by us or a third party. On-site request would be limited to twice in the first 12 months and we would cover reasonable travel costs.

- Evidence retention: 12 months is a hard requirement for us — auditors may need historic artifacts to validate remediation windows. Would Redwood consider making 12 months the standard retention?

- Auditor interviews: We may request short interviews (15–30 minutes) with the operations engineer responsible for a control during a remote verification. Would Redwood accept this under the NDA and with prior scheduling?

If we can get those items confirmed (or get a close counterproposal), procurement can move forward to sign. Happy to do a 30-minute call this week with Rishi + Marissa.

Best,
Elena

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order Form: audit access & security exhibit — request for specifics

Thanks Elena — good points. Proposed compromise below which I hope closes procurement: 

- Notice: We'll accept 15 business days' notice for planned verifications. For urgent incidents that materially affect regulated data flows, CloudScale may request an expedited review; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate but requires mutual agreement on scope, location (remote preferred), and evidence types.

- On-site: Redwood will permit up to two on-site reviews in the first 12 months in connection with high-risk (as defined in the exhibit) engagements; customer covers reasonable travel costs and provides a pre-agreed agenda. Remote verifications and short operations interviews (15–30 minutes) are permitted under NDA and scheduling constraints.

- Evidence retention: Redwood will retain and make available, via secure portal, redacted artifacts and supporting evidence for 12 months following their generation (SOC 2 report availability unchanged). We will not provide raw production logs or exploit payloads.

- Auditor interviews & access: Subject to Redwood's security screening and the auditor NDA, short remote interviews with named ops staff are acceptable; full system access or admin credentials will not be provided.

I attached our most recent SOC 2 and a redacted pen-test summary for reference. If this looks okay, Marissa can issue a tracked redline and I will forward to procurement. Also proposing a 30-minute call Wednesday morning to finalize.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025.pdf (pdf); PenTest-Summary-20251123.pdf (pdf)
